security_audit.summary: Static matches for Ruby backtick execution are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline formatting. The hidden-file and reconnaissance matches are benign project-planning content. Template copy commands present one medium-risk overwrite concern.

remediation.issue: Template copy commands can replace existing project files.
remediation.suggestion: Check whether each destination exists, request confirmation, and use non-clobbering writes or backups before copying templates.

content.value_statement: Complex portfolios hide dependencies, capacity conflicts, and release risks. This skill creates coordinated roadmaps, allocation options, dependency maps, and concise health reports.
actual_capabilities: Maps technical, sequencing, and resource dependencies across software projects.
Builds quarterly, annual, theme-based, and Now-Next-Later roadmaps.
Compares resource allocation options using capacity, priority, and onboarding constraints.
Sequences coordinated releases with checkpoints, monitoring, rollback, and communication plans.
Summarizes portfolio health through status, progress, blockers, utilization, and risk metrics.
Connects projects and initiatives to objectives and measurable key results.
limitations: Recommendations depend on accurate project status, capacity, deadlines, and dependency data.
The skill cannot resolve organizational conflicts or approve staffing and budget changes.
Referenced templates and helper scripts are not included in the audited file.
Shell and file operations require review before execution in a live workspace.

use_cases.title: Plan a Portfolio Roadmap
use_cases.description: Align initiatives with objectives, milestones, capacity, and dependencies for a quarterly planning cycle.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Shared Release
use_cases.description: Sequence dependent service and application releases with checkpoints, rollback plans, monitoring, and stakeholder communication.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Capacity Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare staffing options across competing projects while considering priorities, onboarding time, deadlines, and sustainable utilization.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Portfolio Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these project summaries: {projects}. List priorities, owners, milestones, blockers, and immediate next actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a concise portfolio overview.

prompt_templates.title: Map Project Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Map dependencies among {projects}. Classify each dependency, identify owners and blockers, and show the critical path.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Resource Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Allocate {team_capacity} across {projects}. Compare three options using priority, deadlines, skills, onboarding, utilization, and delivery risk.
prompt_templates.scenario: Support a staffing or capacity decision.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Integrated Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a {planning_horizon} roadmap for {objectives}. Include initiatives, dependencies, capacity, milestones, risks, metrics, review gates, and alternatives.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce an advanced portfolio plan with tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Coordinate releases for an API, web application, and mobile application.
output: Release order: API, web application, then mobile application.
Gate each phase with integration tests, health metrics, and rollback readiness.
Notify stakeholders before rollout and publish daily status during deployment.

output_examples.input: Allocate two new engineers across four active projects.
output: Assign the senior engineer to the fixed-deadline project after confirming mentorship capacity.
Place the junior engineer on lower-risk onboarding work before a planned transfer.
Review velocity, onboarding progress, and schedule impact after four weeks.

output_examples.input: Create a quarterly roadmap for seven projects across three teams.
output: Group projects under strategic themes and connect each theme to measurable objectives.
Mark the critical path, parallel work, team allocation, monthly milestones, and portfolio risks.
Reserve capacity for maintenance, technical debt, and unexpected work.

best_practices: Provide current status, owners, dates, capacity, and dependencies for every project.
Validate recommendations with project leads before changing commitments or staffing.
Review roadmaps and dependency maps regularly as scope, evidence, and constraints change.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize utilization so tightly that teams lack capacity for incidents or unknown work.
Do not assign people across many projects without measuring context-switching costs.
Do not treat a generated roadmap as approval from accountable stakeholders.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide project goals, owners, status, milestones, deadlines, dependencies, team capacity, and known risks.

faq.question: Can this skill create a quarterly roadmap?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize initiatives by objectives, themes, capacity, dependencies, milestones, and success measures.

faq.question: Can it coordinate releases across repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose release order, checkpoints, monitoring, rollback plans, and communication steps from supplied project data.

faq.question: Does it make staffing decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It compares options and impacts, while accountable leaders approve assignments and organizational changes.

faq.question: Will it execute project commands?
faq.answer: The skill includes shell examples, but every command and file change should be reviewed before execution.

faq.question: Are the referenced templates and scripts included?
faq.answer: No. The audited package contains only SKILL.md, so referenced supporting files are unavailable in this version.
